result.title: Learning Probabilistic Logic Programs with Functional Gradient Guided Language Models
result.summary: Declarative logic programs offer a powerful and interpretable abstraction for encoding relational structure and neurosymbolic reasoning, by expressing dependencies as weighted compositional rules. However, inducing them from data remains fundamentally hard, bottlenecked by the combinatorial explosion of symbolic search spaces. LLMs have recently emerged as powerful hypothesis generators, but when used in isolation, they lack the capacity to do systematic inductive reasoning needed to reliably synthesize valid programs that fit complex relational distributions. We introduce grasp (Gradient-boosted Synthesis of Probabilistic logic programs), a neurosymbolic framework that casts relational structure learning as functional gradient boosting in which the weak learner is a first-order rule and the intractable inner search is delegated to an LLM proposal oracle. We evaluate grasp on four relational benchmarks spanning molecular toxicity prediction (Tox21), mutagenesis, and citation matching (Cora), and show that it improves over purely symbolic, neural, and LLM-based baselines, while producing interpretable weighted rule ensembles. By replacing combinatorial search with gradient-guided LLM hypothesis generation, grasp retains boosting guarantees without sacrificing the transparency of symbolic outputs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 grasp，把关系结构学习表述为函数梯度提升，以一阶规则为弱学习器、将难解的内部符号搜索外包给 LLM 作为提案预言机，在分子毒性（Tox21）、致突变与 Cora 引文匹配等基准上报告优于纯符号、神经与 LLM 基线的效果，并输出可解释的加权规则集成。
AI.relevance_reason: 「梯度引导 + LLM 提案 + 弱学习器集成」这一迭代式假设生成与加权机制，可能为 LVR 中推理状态的迭代更新、轨迹贡献分配与候选验证提供方法线索，可供人工核查其是否可迁移到 latent 推理的监督与搜索环节。
